title: Shelter-in-place advisory issued for B.C.'s Pemberton Valley, parts of Squamish as flooding closes roads
summary: Shelter-in-place advisories have been issued in the Pemberton Valley and parts of the District of Squamish as flooding threatens local properties and roads. Líl̓wat Nation expanded an evacuation…

image.caption: Water runs through a field in the Pemberton Meadows area on Thursday. (Erica Van Loon)

blocks.text: British Columbia

Shelter-in-place advisories have been issued in the Pemberton Valley and parts of the District of Squamish as flooding threatens local properties and roads. Líl̓wat Nation expanded an evacuation order for its community Thursday morning.
Evacuation orders also issued for part of Pemberton, Líl̓wat Nation
Shelter-in-place advisories have been issued in the Pemberton Valley and parts of the District of Squamish as flooding threatens local properties and roads.
Residents are told to stay where they are, unless they are covered by an evacuation order. Those under order are told to leave immediately.
The order areas include parts of Líl̓wat Nation and part of the village of Pemberton.
Líl̓wat Nation expanded an evacuation order for its community Thursday morning. It said flooding was occurring along the Green River, which is experiencing "exceptionally high flows."
"The Lillooet River is forecast to continue rising for several more hours. The Birkenhead is flowing near record levels," the order reads.

The Líl̓wat Nation has EXPANDED the Evacuation Order from Kwetsa7 along the Lillooet River corridor to Lillooet Lake due to flooding. Flood waters are a threat to life & safety. Go to Úll̓us Community Complex. If water blocks your route, do not attempt to cross. Move to a safe location on higher ground & call for assistance. For immediate danger or rescue call 911. More info: https://t.co/zGyQznHOE9 #BCFlood #BC—EmergencyInfoBC
The nation says sections of Lillooet Lake Road had about six inches to one foot of water flowing over it.
People are urged not to walk or drive through floodwater.
The nation has a muster point and reception centre open at Úll̓us Community Complex.

In Pemberton, an evacuation order covers the Pemberton Regional Airport, the B.C. Wildfire Service base, golf course facilities, an animal shelter and a small number of residential properties.
A reception centre is open at the Pemberton and District Community Centre.
The entire village is under evacuation alert, as well as properties within the Electoral Area C portion of the Pemberton Valley.
The valley is also covered by a shelter-in-place advisory.
The Squamish-Lillooet Regional District (SLRD) says sections of Pemberton Meadows Road and Highway 99 are impassable.

Canada Post issued a red delivery service alert due to the flooding impacting Pemberton. It said in a statement that all mail and parcels destined for the village will be held at a Canada Post facility until postal services can resume.

blocks.text: In the District of Squamish, a shelter-in-place advisory covers the Paradise Valley, Sunwolf Lodge and Cheekye Ranch area due to flooding downstream of the Cheakamus Dam (Daisy Lake).
Squamish Valley Road was closed at the Pilchuck Bailey Bridge due to flooding concerns on Thursday. (Troy Charles/CBC)
The district said Paradise Valley Road is closed at the Paradise Valley Bailey Bridge and Squamish Valley Road is closed at the Pilchuck Bailey Bridge.
"River levels are expected to peak today and begin to drop as rainfall from the storm works its way through the river system," it said in a morning update.
More rain on the weekend
Squamish Mayor Sean Easton said the district is used to big storms and heavy rainfall, and is preparing for another weather system on the weekend.

"We're trying to respond in this moment, but then also trying to look at it and make sure that we're ready for the next storm moving through," he said. "It's unclear what that storm looks like, as far as amounts at this time."
He added the district's emergency operations centre is monitoring the situation.
Squamish Mayor Sean Easton said the Sea-to-Sky community is bracing for more storms on the weekend. (Mike Zimmer/CBC)

Pemberton Valley and parts of the South Coast are under a flood warning, with the River Forecast Centre saying river levels there "have been rising rapidly since late Tuesday night" and are expected to continue to rise into Thursday.
The centre has also issued flood warnings for the Kingcome River and Vancouver Island.
High streamflow advisories are in place for southern Vancouver Island, the Fraser Valley, Fraser Canyon and Chilcotin.
Environment Canada has rainfall warnings in effect for east, inland and west Vancouver Island, as well as parts of the Sunshine Coast.
